plain_what: The model is a table of small integer vectors plus a few routing choices. To learn, the machine tries every legal rotation of one table entry, replays the examples under each, keeps the one with the lowest integer loss, and commits it only if it strictly helps. No gradients, no floating point, no matrix products.
how_it_works: State: a shared integer codebook (token -> 8D vector blocks, each block one of 16 roots of one E8 anchor orbit), a categorical frame per route stage (one of 64 signed-axis group elements) and optional ternary read gates. Forward: a token window is read by Route (the transformed query is compared with fixed FBS branch roots, never leaf contents), Flock{kept} or Relation. A shared writer gives each token a product cell from the root indices of its first and last blocks (256 cells), ranks cells by L1 address distance, scans up to K kept cells and scores token L1 distance. Loss numerator = 8*token_hinge + width*address_hinge over 8*width (objective A), or an occupied-cell rank variant (R). Learning step for one coordinate (a VectorBlock, a Route frame or a Gate): replay read and writer for identity plus the 15 bivector moves over rows fixed eligible by the baseline; choose the minimum integer cost, ties to identity, then lowest resulting port; apply only a strictly improving move and validate. The rows_v1 kernel computes the baseline once per row and each virtual move once per (row, lane), reproducing the serial losses exactly. BVG-K scores K coordinates per launch and commits a block only if its joint loss beats the best single move.
geometry: E8 anchor-orbit roots (16 per 8D block, not the full 240), SpiralCore 64-element signed-axis group with action/composition/inverse tables and BFS transport, ternary FBS children/frontier, integer L1 and Hamming distances, bivector moves, product cells from first/last block root indices, icosian/quaternion actions only as design intent.

status_reason: This is the learning law of the only current model path, crates/uor-r4-discrete (docs/labs/discrete-geometric-learning-2026-10-13, docs/architecture.md). It trained a pilot and four K16 runs, and the pilot still shows no language gain (docs/labs/k16-outcome-call-2026-10-19). Training stays HELD pending owner release.

rule_compat.D11: The model is already integer: table, routes and gates are integers, and reads, writer and loss use integer add, compare and table lookups. The served form is the same snapshot, so there is no float to discretize. A served D11 engine for this model does not exist yet, and no export gap or tokens/s has been measured.
rule_compat.D23: No softmax, exp, softplus, sigmoid or tanh anywhere. Choice is an integer argmin with an explicit tie rule, and the objective is an integer hinge (docs/labs/discrete-geometric-learning-2026-10-13).
rule_compat.D30: No matmul or GEMM. Distances are integer L1 and Hamming over 8D blocks, and moves are group-table lookups. D29 scans the compiled CUDA module (scripts/check_native_cuda_vendor.rs).
rule_compat.D32_D37: This is the D32 law (discrete, GPU-only, no float). D37 later allowed offline float training, but this module stays integer and a float path would need its own scanned module and a reported export gap. All model operations are GPU-only, with no host fallback.

open_questions: Which acceptance criterion keeps accepted moves from trading admission for within-list rank?
Can cell assignment by address structure (rather than 256 evenly spread cells) raise admission at K=8 without re-creating aliasing?
Does a speedup of about 56x (rows) and 8-16x (BVG-K) change what dose is affordable enough to settle the question?
Is a Route/Relation read with learned frames actually better than the frozen-zero control once admission is held fixed?
How large is the gap between the integer win and an offline float credit law on the same geometry (D37)?
